correctness.rationale: Formal-power-series units are detected by the constant term. Under 2 not in U(R), the constant-term fibers are infinite independent sets and base edges become complete bipartite links. A total dominating set of the finite base lifts, while any finite minimum dominating set upstairs projects to a total dominating set by choosing an unselected vertex in each infinite fiber.

evidence: Afkhami--Khosh-Ahang (2013) gives the constant-term adjacency criterion for R[[x]], an equivalence for the whole unit set being dominating, and infinite complete bipartite subgraphs, but no minimum-domination formula.
Kiani--Maimani--Pournaki--Yassemi (2015) explicitly restricts to finite commutative rings and studies domination/total domination there.
Chelvam--Kathirvel--Balamurugan (2020) treats generalized unit/unitary Cayley graphs of finite rings, a different graph.
Du--Gan (2025) explicitly studies domination parameters for finite commutative rings; its rendered introduction cites the 2013 power-series paper as separate prior work.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The source most capable of implying the claim is the 2013 power-series paper. Its inspected power-series remarks stop at adjacency and a non-minimal dominating-set equivalence, leaving the minimum transfer unproved.

value.rationale: The theorem reduces domination of an infinite algebraic graph to total domination of a finite base graph. It yields exact values for every finite local ring with characteristic-two residue field and accommodates nonlocal examples with larger values, so it is a reusable structural principle rather than a one-off computation.
